- **New Components**:
  - Tab component for grouping related codeblocks in tabs

#### **Utilities Added**

- `formatDate(date)` → Consistent date formatting
- `parseBaseURL()` → Parses `.env` base URLs into segments

#### **Build Modifications**

- Updated commands to preprocess `.mdx` via Velite

#### **Known Gaps**

⚠️ **Pending Improvements**:

body:
# Changes

Fixes #1881
Fixes #1882

Updates in preparation of v0.16.

- KinD from v0.26.0 to v0.27.0
- ko from v0.17.1 to v0.18.0
- Supported k8s versions: old v1.29 to v1.32, new v1.30 to v1.33
- go.mod k8s dependencies: v0.30 to v0.32
- go.mod controller-runtime: v0.18 to v0.20
- go.mod tekton pipelines: v0.68.1 to v1.0.0
- controller-gen: v0.15.0 to v0.17.3
- e2e tested k8s versions: old v1.29.12 and v1.32.0, new v1.30.10 and v1.33.0
- Minimum supported Tekton version: v0.62 instead of v0.59
- e2e tested Tekton version: old v0.59.5 and v0.68.1, new 0.62.9 and v1.0.0

I had to make the inline VolumeSource on the build strategy optional as otherwise controller-gen was creating a required field with an empty name (`""`) in the OpenAPI spec which one cannot fulfill. Not sure if that is a bug or a feature. Inline structs have no field in the JSON as such they cannot really themselves be required but only properties inside them could be. And while changing that I noticed that we forgot to provide any description for the fields in the build strategy spec, so I added them.

Integration tests had to be refactored, see https://github.com/shipwright-io/build/pull/1879#issuecomment-2868997684.

I will change branch protected settings regarding required checks when approved so that the automatic merge happens.

body:
A2AJava has built-in support for Model Context Protocol (MCP) using intuitive Java annotations, this project serves as an excellent starting point for building MCP-compliant servers in Java that are also cross compliant with Google A2A protocol. Developers can quickly define, expose, and orchestrate agent skills and actions within a shared context, enabling powerful, multi-agent workflows with minimal boilerplate



## Description
This submission introduces a Java-based server framework (A2AJava) that provides seamless integration between Google’s A2A protocol and the Model Context Protocol (MCP). It allows developers to register annotated Java methods as MCP-compatible tools and resources, auto-generating task interfaces and exposing them to LLM-based clients.

The project demonstrates task execution, context sharing, and skill orchestration using lightweight annotations and Spring Boot, making it ideal for scalable agent development in Java environments

## Motivation and Context
There is currently limited support for building MCP servers in Java, despite its widespread enterprise adoption. A2AJava fills this gap by enabling Java developers to create and deploy agent-capable MCP servers quickly and efficiently, reducing boilerplate and lowering the barrier to entry. It also bridges A2A and MCP, promoting greater interoperability between AI tools and services.

## How Has This Been Tested?
Tested using local LLM clients including OpenAI and Claude via Tools4AI framework.
Sample use case: Airline ticket booking agent that receives structured tasks, processes them via annotated Java methods, and returns contextual responses.
Tested multipart message handling, tool discovery, and task chaining.

## Additional context
A2AJava enables seamless context sharing between the A2A protocol and Model Context Protocol (MCP) in Java-based applications. It also supports intelligent task dispatching, making it ideal for multi-agent workflows, dynamic task routing, and context-driven skill activation. The framework integrates effortlessly with Kafka, REST APIs, and local LLM clients, leveraging Java reflection to reduce boilerplate. With built-in annotations like Agent and Action, and support for dynamic task state transitions, A2AJava makes it incredibly easy to build a fully A2A- and MCP-compliant server in Java — often in under an hour, from the ground up.

body:
The UI Tax stuff tested on Poll and Land Tax do display, but keys are partially wiped somewhere. I gonna expand that another time. 

Tax Code has been "balanced" to make Landtax and Polltax "exist" properly. 
Also simplified the TaxCostCode significantly. Removing >1 Million of calculations per Census, if not significantly more. 
In Core added new Helper functions to make the Code cleaner but also moved calculations outside of the Taxes, so the majority of taxes do not calculate the same stuff again and again, instead pull it out of a tmp. 
Also got rid of most "balance" factors and consolidated them into one single balance factor which is used when the taxcost calculation is finalized. Therefore it offers a simple way of buffing or nerfing a Mana Cost. 
I am not sure why PollTaxes were still applied, even though they were bringing it almost no ducats. That must be some kind of odd thing in the weighting of the Tax Ratios when deciding what Tax to use. I could not identify the root cause for this, but after adjusting polltax costs and polltax base tax ratio, the taxes were applied similarly, but now with an actually ducat "yield". Either I accidently fixed it by just going over it without noticing it (in case it was just an error in decimals, so it no longer disappears in the calculations) or a code bug. 
Overall Tax income at start is up about 15-50% depending on how feudal you are. Noble Dues are larger now, therefore feudal realms do have a better income from relying on their nobles :) + 5-10% higher income from Poll and Land Tax Improvements. 

In Future this will be combined with the State Property Branch which will then shut down any State Property "exploits" and you actually have to care about Taxation!
